title: The Rise of the Interactive Tech Support Scam Ads
description: Online Tech Support Scams are becoming a large problem for computer users. When users encounter these windows that state there is something wrong with their computer, they may panic and call the advertised number where they are sold products and services they do not need.

asr.full_text: Hi there! You're seeing this page because it looks like you have pop-up ads turned on. Would you like some help disabling them now? Okay, great. I'm going to provide you with my direct phone number. Are you able to call right now? Great. Please call the number displayed on your screen and press one when prompted to speak with. Me directly. Thank you.

textual.context: The title and description frame the material as discussion of tech support scam ads, while the ASR is phrased as an apparent support-ad script; whether it is being promoted, quoted or demonstrated is not fully established by these records.
textual.potential_relevance: The combination of an apparent computer-support claim, an immediate phone-call instruction and a stated connection to selling unnecessary products or services is a concrete mechanism for later contextual assessment.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish whether any products were actually sold, whether the number was displayed, who operated it, or whether the ASR represents an actual advertisement, quotation or demonstration.

visual.observation: A browser page displays an alert stating that a Windows 7 computer has popup ads enabled, asks whether the viewer can call, presents YES/NO prompts, and later displays "Call Immediately" with the toll-free number 1-877-886-9052. The page also shows system and ISP-style information and "Trusted Verify"/"Secure Safe" badges.
visual.context: The call prompt and technical-support-style claims appear within a browser page featuring a presenter; whether this is a demonstration, warning, or live offer is unclear from the sampled frames.
visual.potential_relevance: A technical-support-style warning and system-identity claims are linked to an urgent request for the viewer to make a phone call, which is a concretely described support-contact mechanism for review.
visual.limitations: These sampled frames cannot establish whether the displayed page, phone number, system information, ISP claim, or security badges are authentic, nor whether anyone called or experienced an outcome.
